meta.what: Russian private (non-central-bank) assets frozen abroad, per holding country and year 2022-2026, and the yearly return those assets would have earned for their Russian owners without the freeze ('return lost', same rule as frozen_assets.json). Separately, as a marker not in the totals: western investors' income blocked in Russia on type-C accounts, per owner country.
meta.units: EUR bn nominal; rates as fractions a year; 2022 = 28 Feb-31 Dec (10/12), 2026 = Jan-Aug (8/12). Ranges about 90%.
meta.method: return_lost[y] = stock_central[y] x financial_share x blended_rate[y] x year_fraction[y]; blended_rate = currency mix x the per-currency short rates of frozen_assets.json (rates_by_currency_pct; CHF added here). Yachts, villas, art and company stakes earn no money-market return, so only the financial share counts. Low/high combine the relative errors of stock, financial share and rate in quadrature; the low end is floored at low x low x low. The stock itself is not counted.
meta.status: Research input for round 39, not wired into the pipeline.
no_double_count: Bank of Russia reserves: all national figures used here are the authorities' private/sanctioned-person figures that exclude the central bank (SECO, OFSI, Belgian Treasury 'frozen assets' vs 'blocked transactions', France's 23.7bn less 22.8bn, Germany's 5.32bn less 0.21bn).

Euroclear's own income: interest Euroclear earns on private sanctioned cash (about EUR 13bn: EUR 193bn sanctioned on the balance sheet against about 180bn for the Bank of Russia, CEO, Oct 2025) is Russia's lost return counted here once. The EU windfall contribution is levied only on income from Bank of Russia balances, so none of it is this money. The Belgian corporate tax on Euroclear's Russia-related profit (which also covers private cash) is already taken in full off the reserves line (BEL_EUROCLEAR_TAX), so nothing more is taken off here.

frozen_assets.json gives Belgium's immobilised reserves a high end of 192bn; above about 186bn that would include private cash. Builder: cap that high end at 186 or accept a small overlap (at most EUR 0.2-0.3bn a year in the high end).
seized marker (company_flows): Russia's seizures of western assets are the mirror image; type-C balances are a separate marker and do not include seized companies.

rates_added_pct.note: SNB policy rate averages (low), up to 1-2-year Confederation yields plus a spread (high); judgement. Other currencies: frozen_assets.json rates_by_currency_pct.

BEL_csd.name: Belgium (Euroclear: securities blocked through NSD, sanctioned Russian banks)
BEL_csd.basis: Belgian Treasury: EUR 50bn frozen in Belgium (Commission document via Politico, Nov 2022, CBR reserves listed separately); EUR 58.7bn of frozen assets 'mainly securities' besides EUR 191.9bn of blocked transactions (Treasury director De Geest, Le Soir, early 2023); EUR 65bn frozen assets in Feb 2025, of which EUR 55bn securities that passed through the sanctioned NSD (mostly unsanctioned Russian investors) and about EUR 10bn of sanctioned Russian banks (OCCRP). The EUR 191-193bn of blocked transactions is the Bank of Russia's position and stays in frozen_assets.json. Low ends allow for the Bank of Russia's statement that about half of the RUB 5.7tn blocked at Euroclear and Clearstream had been unblocked by early 2025. The figure is taken to include Belgium's EUR 3.5bn of sanctioned persons' assets reported to the Commission (Dec 2022), so that figure is not added.
BEL_csd.host_rule: as reserves: one third to the host, two thirds to EU members by EU-aid share

LUX_csd.name: Luxembourg (Clearstream: securities blocked through NSD)
LUX_csd.basis: Residual guess: the Bank of Russia put Russian investors' assets blocked at Euroclear and Clearstream at RUB 5.7tn at end-Nov 2022 (about EUR 85-90bn at RUB 63-66 per euro), over 20% of it retail; Belgium's Treasury accounts for EUR 50-59bn in 2022-23; Clearstream is taken as the rest less a margin. About half of the 2022 total was unblocked by early 2025 (Nabiullina) and RUB 0.4tn more in 2025; the path follows that. No Luxembourg or Clearstream figure is published.
LUX_csd.host_rule: as reserves: one third to the host, two thirds to EU members by EU-aid share

LUX_nat.name: Luxembourg (banks and funds, sanctioned persons)
LUX_nat.basis: Finance ministry: EUR 2.5bn (Mar 2022), 4.3bn (Jun 2022, deposits and securities of over 1,100 persons and 90 entities), 5.5bn (22 Dec 2022); the Commission's member-state list had 2.5bn (Dec 2022), which sets the low end. No later figure found; held flat. Could overlap with Clearstream if the ministry counts NSD-linked positions (not stated).
LUX_nat.host_rule: full to the host (like France's or Switzerland's reserves)

DEU.name: Germany
DEU.basis: EUR 2.2bn in the Commission's Dec 2022 list; EUR 5.32bn frozen in all (Finance Ministry via Welt am Sonntag, 2025), of which the Bank of Russia's 'small three-digit million amount' (about 0.21) is taken off. Includes a EUR 720m sanctioned-bank account now in confiscation proceedings (Frankfurt, Oct 2025). No register published yet.

ITA.name: Italy
ITA.basis: Guardia di Finanza list over EUR 1.7bn (late 2022); EUR 2.3bn in the Commission's Dec 2022 list; press up to EUR 3bn. Mostly yachts and villas (Scheherazade about EUR 650m), so a low financial share.

IRL.name: Ireland
IRL.basis: EUR 1.72bn (Jun 2022), 1.8bn (Commission, Dec 2022), over 1.9bn (government answers to the Dail, Mar and May 2024); financial institutions only; Irish institutions hold no Bank of Russia assets.

AUT.name: Austria
AUT.basis: About EUR 2bn at end-2022 (Finance Minister Brunner; 1.8 in the Commission's list), down to about 1.5bn after exemptions and exchange-rate effects (DSN, confirmed by the OeNB).

FRA.name: France
FRA.basis: Treasury list (2022): EUR 23.7bn frozen, of which 22.8bn Bank of Russia (in frozen_assets.json), so about 0.9bn private, with 33 properties worth EUR 574m; EUR 1.3bn in the Commission's Dec 2022 list. Mostly property and yachts, so a low financial share. No later total found.

ESP.name: Spain
ESP.basis: EUR 41m (Commissioner Reynders, Sep 2022) and EUR 1.0bn (Commission list, Dec 2022): the two do not reconcile. Yachts and property weigh heavily.

NLD.name: Netherlands
NLD.basis: EUR 660m frozen since the invasion; just under EUR 100m left by Oct 2024 after over EUR 560m was released with the foreign ministry's permission (letter to parliament, Oct 2024).

CYP.name: Cyprus
CYP.basis: About EUR 1.5bn (Finance Minister, Jan 2023); EUR 1.3bn (Foreign Minister Kombos, Jan 2025: 901m investment firms, 307m administrative service providers, 90m other); EUR 1.2bn (Oct 2025).

GBR.name: United Kingdom
GBR.basis: OFSI: GBP 18.39bn of financial assets under the Russia regime (annual review 2021-22, to Oct 2022); GBP 10.2bn in the 2023 frozen-asset review; GBP 22.5bn in the 2024 review (current values, excluding assets that cannot be valued; includes assets held abroad under UK jurisdiction); in-year reporting GBP 25.03bn (2023-24) and 28.7bn (May 2025) at values when frozen. Central = GBP 16, 14, 22.5, 23, 23bn. Converted at about 1.17, 1.15, 1.18, 1.17, 1.15 EUR per GBP. Includes sanctioned Russian banks and state companies; whether any Bank of Russia money is in it is not stated (the Bank of Russia is under transaction prohibitions rather than an asset freeze).

CHE.name: Switzerland
CHE.basis: SECO, financial assets of sanctioned persons and companies, kept separate from the Bank of Russia's CHF 7.45bn: CHF 7.5bn (Dec 2022), 5.8bn (end-2023, after valuation losses), 7.4bn (Apr 2025 and 1 Jun 2025), 8.5bn (1 Jun 2026, SECO spokesman via Izvestia). Central CHF 7.0, 6.6, 6.6, 7.4, 8.3bn at about 1.0, 1.03, 1.05, 1.07, 1.07 EUR per CHF. Property (14 buildings), cars and art are not valued and not included.

USA.name: United States
USA.basis: No US total is published. REPO members together blocked or froze over USD 58bn of sanctioned Russians' assets by Mar 2023 (30bn by Jun 2022). Taking off the EU (about EUR 21-24bn), the UK (about GBP 18bn) and small Canadian, Australian and Japanese amounts leaves about USD 5-12bn for the US and Japan; KleptoCapture's criminal restraints were only USD 0.5bn+ (Feb 2023). Central EUR 5bn; a guess.

JPN.name: Japan
JPN.basis: Not published; a REPO member. Guess from the REPO residual.

CAN.name: Canada
CAN.basis: RCMP: CAD 185m frozen plus CAD 473m of blocked transactions (the latter only in the high end).

unallocated_eu.name: EU, not split (Finland, Baltic states, Poland, Czechia, Sweden, Greece, Malta, Portugal and others)
unallocated_eu.basis: Commission total (EUR 18.9bn Dec 2022; 24.1bn mid-2023; 'more than EUR 28bn' on its page updated Oct 2026) less the member states above (Belgium counted at its Commission figure of 3.5 for this subtraction, Luxembourg at 2.5). Finland EUR 187m (Jan 2023). Not assigned.

totals_2022_2026.note: Sum of country ranges (fully correlated), unallocated EU block excluded. Before the pipeline's x0.8 on the low end.

map_effect_proposed_rule.rule: csd component: one third to the host, two thirds to EU members by EU-aid share (as reserves); national component: full to the host; low end x0.8 (as reserves). Totals 2022-Aug 2026, EUR bn; % of average 2022-2024 GDP (site/data.json gdp). existing_frozen_line_central = today's 'Russian money frozen' line.

type_c_marker.what: Roubles owed to holders from 'unfriendly' countries (dividends, coupons, redemptions, sale proceeds) that Russia pays only into type-C accounts (decree 95, 5 Mar 2022), which cannot leave Russia. A marker, not in the totals (like 'seized'): Russia took it; the country did not choose it.
type_c_marker.stock_basis: End-period stock, RUB tn. Official: over RUB 280bn (Bank of Russia, early Nov 2022; its only disclosure). Interfax sources: close to RUB 0.6tn at end-2022. Sberbank's Dzhabarov (NAUFOR, May 2025): Russian companies paid RUB 1.4tn into type-C accounts in 2022-2024 and the largest dividend payers will add RUB 704bn in 2025. Deposit Insurance Agency: its deposited funds rose from RUB 19.7bn to 1.184tn in 2023 (Moscow Times link to type-C, not confirmed). Releases are small (asset-exchange schemes, RUB 10.6bn bought back by non-residents in two rounds). 2026 adds the 2025-year dividends (Sberbank's record payout, about a quarter to type-C). Medvedev's 'USD 300bn' (Dec 2025) is not used: no source, and it is near the whole FDI stock.
type_c_marker.deposit_regime_2026: Decree 377/2026 (Jun 2026) put foreign nationals' bank deposits into the regime; decree 550/2026 (Aug 2026) took most of them out again. Not in the figures.
type_c_marker.interest_kept_note: type-C balances earn little or nothing; interest_kept_by_russia = average stock x Bank of Russia average key rate: the free funding Russia's banks and issuers get. It is a gain to Russia only while the rouble does not fall by as much.
type_c_marker.allocation: By the holder's 2021 portfolio position in Russian securities (IMF Portfolio Investment Positions by Counterpart Economy, formerly CPIS, end-2021; api.imf.org dataflow IMF.STA:PIP 5.0.0): equity + 0.5 x debt, 'unfriendly' holders only. Direct-investment parents' dividends (also type-C) are not in this key; Cyprus, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Cayman Islands partly hold for Russians (round-tripping) and for US funds, so their shares overstate their own residents.
